A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effective theory approach is a powerful method to analyze parity-violating NN scattering at low energies.
parity-violating NN scattering at low energies is a rich source of information on the parity-violating interactions of the nucleon.
the parity-violating asymmetries in the 2 S 1 / 2, 1 D 2, and 3 D 3 partial waves are the most promising observables to extract the leading-order parity-violating NN couplings.
The main takeaway from our work is that
parity-violating nucleonic interactions can be described by a small number of coefficients that can be determined by measuring a small number of observables.
the parity-violating NN scattering asymmetry is sensitive to the combination of the coefficients of the Lagrangian that is most difficult to access in other low-energy parity-violating experiments.
, while there are many observables that can be measured, there are not enough to determine all of the coefficients in the leading-order parity-violating NN Lagrangian.
